useCase.name: Define what each role may reach, and enforce it on every request rather than by hiding menu items

intent.name: role.create
intent.summary: Create a role and choose the permissions it holds, module by module.
routesHere: create a Coordinator role that can approve results and see attendance

routesHere.text: naya role banana hai — Coordinator, results approve kar sake
routesHere.gloss: we want a new role — Coordinator, able to approve results

routesHere.text: Accounts ka role bana dein fee module ki permissions ke saath
routesHere.gloss: create an Accounts role with the fee module permissions

routesHere.text: ek role chahiye jo sirf dekh sake, kuch badal na sake
routesHere.gloss: we want a role that can only view and change nothing

routesHere: set up a role for the exam office

request.text: ye role bilkul mita dein
request.gloss: delete this role completely

routesElsewhere.note: There is no delete. The audit trail references the role, and every entry recording what somebody did under it would point at nothing (BR-8, E9).

request.text: is user ko ye role de dein
request.gloss: give this user this role

routesElsewhere.goesTo: branch.user.assign — UC-23-02, or branch.user.role.change where they are already assigned there.
routesElsewhere.note: The role a user holds is held on their **branch assignment**, not on the user, so one person may hold different roles at different branches (BR-7). Assigning is done at the branch — by the Super Admin, or by the School Admin of that branch where the permission is delegated, and then only within their own branch, only to roles at or below their own, and only to permissions released to that branch (BR-2, BR-3, E2, E3, E4).

request.text: ek nayi permission bana dein
request.gloss: create a new permission

routesElsewhere.note: Permissions are defined by the system and are not created by anybody — not by the Super Admin either. A role holds a set of the permissions that exist (BR-1).

request.text: menu se ye option chhupa dein
request.gloss: hide this option from the menu

routesElsewhere.note: Hiding a menu item is decoration over an address anybody can type. The check runs on the server on every request, and a request without permission is refused whether it came from the menu or from a typed address (BR-4, BR-5, E5, A3).

steps.note: One step. The role and its permission set are recorded, and nobody holds it until a user is assigned to it at a branch (BR-2, BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A duplicate name refuses the role, and a permission that does not exist is asked about rather than invented.
plan.atomicity: One write. **The role does nothing until somebody holds it**, and holding it happens on a branch assignment rather than here (BR-2, BR-7).

operations.name: role.create
operations.idempotencyKey: role name, since a role name is unique and a double press must not leave two roles the school cannot tell apart
operations.purpose: Create a role with its permission set.

parameters.name: name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters, unique (E1). The school's own name for the role — and whether roles are defined once across the group or separately per branch is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2).

parameters.name: permission_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such permission exists. Permissions are defined by the system and are not created (BR-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the permissions that match with the module each belongs to — two permissions in different modules often read almost the same.

parameters.notes: The permissions, chosen module by module. **Permissions themselves are defined by the system and are not created by anybody** — a permission that does not exist cannot be invented to fit a request (BR-1).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The role and what it can reach.

fields.name: role_id
fields.description: The role.

fields.name: permissions
fields.description: What it holds, by module (BR-1).

fields.name: users_holding_it
fields.description: Zero. A role does nothing until a user is assigned to it at a branch (BR-2, BR-7).

fields.name: released_to_branches
fields.description: None yet. Until a permission is released to a branch, a School Admin there cannot grant it (BR-3).

fields.name: assignable_by
fields.description: The Super Admin always, and a School Admin where delegated — then only within their own branch and only to roles at or below their own (BR-2, BR-3).

fields.name: enforced_where
fields.description: On the server, on every request, without exception. Not by hiding menu items (BR-4, BR-5, E7).

errors.meaning: A role of the same name exists.

planningRules.rule: Never invent a permission. They are defined by the system and created by nobody, so a request for something the permission list does not contain is answered by saying so rather than by picking the nearest thing (BR-1).
Never widen the permission set. Each permission added is something everybody who ever holds this role can reach, and it is far easier to grant than to take back (BR-1).
Say that the role does nothing yet. It is held on a branch assignment, and until somebody is assigned to it at a branch it grants nothing to anybody (BR-2, BR-7).

Never describe hiding a menu item as restricting access. The check runs on the server on every request, and what is hidden is still reachable by typing the address — that is the distinction the whole use case turns on (BR-4, BR-5, E5).
Say that nothing has been released to any branch. Until the Super Admin releases a permission to a branch, no School Admin there can grant it to anybody (BR-3).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A role created in error is deactivated once nobody holds it — and refused while anybody does, since a user with no role can do nothing (BR-8, E8, A5). It is never deleted, because the audit trail references it (E9).

request.text: Coordinator ka role bana dein jo results approve kar sake aur attendance dekh sake
request.gloss: create a Coordinator role that can approve results and see attendance

inputs.name: Coordinator
inputs.permission_ids: $request.permissions_phrase → the two named, confirmed against the permission list

resolvedPlans.outcome: Confirm the exact permissions before creating — "see attendance" matches more than one permission in the attendance module and they are not the same thing. After: report that the role holds two permissions, that nobody holds it yet, and that no School Admin can grant it at any branch until the Super Admin releases those permissions to that branch.

request.text: ek role bana dein jo sab kuch dekh sake lekin kuch badal na sake
request.gloss: create a role that can see everything and change nothing

inputs.name: asked
inputs.permission_ids: $request.permissions_phrase → every view permission, listed back for confirmation

steps.note: The set is read back rather than assembled quietly (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: List what "everything" would include before creating it — every view permission across every module, including salaries, safeguarding notes and the audit trail, each of which is a permission in its own right. A read-only role that can see everything is still a role that can see everything, and it is easier to grant than to take back.

intent.name: role.permissions.update
intent.summary: Add or remove permissions on a role. Everybody holding it is affected at once.
routesHere: give the Coordinator role permission to see the fee ledger

routesHere.text: Coordinator role mein fee ledger ki permission bhi daal dein
routesHere.gloss: add the fee ledger permission to the Coordinator role too

routesHere.text: is role se salary dekhne ki permission hata dein
routesHere.gloss: remove the salary viewing permission from this role

routesHere.text: is role ki permissions kam kar dein

routesHere: trim the permissions on the exam office role

request.text: sirf ek user ke liye permission barha dein
request.gloss: increase the permission for one user only

routesElsewhere.note: Permissions are held by the role, not by the person. Changing them here changes what **everybody** holding the role can reach — a single person needing something different needs a different role (BR-1, BR-7).

request.text: nayi permission bana dein
request.gloss: create a new permission

routesElsewhere.note: Permissions are defined by the system and created by nobody (BR-1).

request.text: apni khud ki role administration hata dein
request.gloss: remove your own role administration

routesElsewhere.note: The Super Admin cannot revoke their own ability to administer roles, since nobody could then restore it (BR-9, E10).

steps.note: One step, and it takes effect on the next request every holder makes — the check runs on the server on every request (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A permission that does not exist is asked about rather than invented, and an attempt to remove the Super Admin's own role administration refuses the whole change (E10).
plan.atomicity: One write, and it changes what every user holding the role can reach from their next request onward (BR-4). Nobody is signed out and nothing warns them.

operations.name: role.permissions.update
operations.idempotencyKey: role_id + the permissions added and removed, so a double press does not record the same change twice
operations.purpose: Add or remove permissions on a role.

parameters.name: role_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No role of that name exists.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the roles that match with how many users hold each and how many permissions each carries.

parameters.notes: The role, named the way the school names it.

parameters.name: add_permission_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such permission exists. Permissions are defined by the system (BR-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the permissions that match with the module each belongs to.

parameters.notes: Permissions being added. Each one is something **everybody** holding this role can now reach (BR-1).

parameters.name: remove_permission_ids

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the permissions the role currently holds.

parameters.notes: Permissions being removed. Each one is something everybody holding this role will stop being able to reach on their next request (BR-4).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What changed and who it changes it for.

fields.name: role_id
fields.description: The role.

fields.name: added
fields.description: Permissions now held.

fields.name: removed
fields.description: Permissions no longer held.

fields.name: users_affected
fields.description: **Everybody holding this role**, at every branch. They are not signed out and nothing tells them (BR-2, BR-7).

fields.name: takes_effect
fields.description: On each holder's next request. The check runs on the server on every request, so there is no cached permission to wait out (BR-4).

fields.name: released_permissions_now_grantable
fields.description: Added permissions already released to a branch, which a School Admin there can now grant to others (BR-3).

fields.name: permissions_now_held
fields.description: What the role carries in total after the change. Nothing here removes a permission that is no longer needed unless somebody names it (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The Super Admin attempted to revoke their own role administration.

planningRules.rule: Say how many people this changes it for. A permission added to a role is added to everybody holding it at every branch at once, and the request usually comes from one person's problem (BR-2, BR-7).
Say that a removal bites immediately and silently. The check runs on the server on every request, so somebody mid-task loses access on their next click with no warning and no sign-out (BR-4, BR-5).
Never invent a permission to fit the request. They are defined by the system, and the nearest-sounding one in another module is a different permission (BR-1).
Say what the role now carries in total. Nothing takes a permission back on its own, so a role only ever grows unless somebody names what should come off (BR-1).
Never remove the Super Admin's own role administration. Nobody could restore it, and the refusal is the last safeguard rather than an obstacle (BR-9, E10).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: There is no undo. Removing a permission again is another change and both are on the audit trail — and anything anybody reached in between, they reached (BR-4).

request.text: Coordinator role mein fee ledger dekhne ki permission daal dein
request.gloss: add the fee ledger viewing permission to the Coordinator role

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, 14 users hold the Coordinator role across two branches.

steps.note: One permission, to everybody who holds the role (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Before adding: this gives the fee ledger to all 14 coordinators at both campuses, not to the one who asked. If only one person needs it, a different role is the route. After: it takes effect on each of their next requests — nobody is signed out and nobody is told — and the role now carries 12 permissions in total.

request.text: is role se salary dekhne ki permission hata dein, foran
request.gloss: remove the salary viewing permission from this role, immediately

steps.note: Removal bites on the next request (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Removed. It takes effect on the next request each holder makes — there is no cached permission to wait out, and somebody with a salary screen open right now will be refused the moment they touch it. Nothing warns them, and nothing takes back what has already been seen.

intent.name: permission.branch.release
intent.summary: Release a permission to a branch, so that branch's School Admin may grant it.
routesHere: release the fee ledger permission to the Johar Town branch

routesHere.text: ye permission Johar Town branch ko release kar dein
routesHere.gloss: release this permission to the Johar Town branch

routesHere.text: School Admin ko ye permission dene ki ijazat de dein
routesHere.gloss: let the School Admin be able to grant this permission

routesHere: let the branch grant the attendance permissions themselves

request.text: School Admin khud release kar lein
request.gloss: let the School Admin release it themselves

routesElsewhere.note: A School Admin cannot grant themselves or anybody else a permission the Super Admin has not released to that branch. Releasing is the Super Admin's (BR-3, E4).

request.text: sab branches ko de dein
request.gloss: release it to all the branches

routesElsewhere.goesTo: Possible, and say what it means.
routesElsewhere.note: Each branch it is released to is a branch whose School Admin can hand this permission to anybody at or below their own role, without asking anybody (BR-2, BR-3).

steps.note: One step. It does not grant the permission to anybody — it makes it grantable at that branch by its own School Admin (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A permission the role does not hold cannot be released for it, and a branch nobody matches is asked about rather than assumed.
plan.atomicity: One write. **Nobody gains anything by this** — it changes who may hand the permission out, not who holds it (BR-3).

operations.name: permission.branch.release
operations.idempotencyKey: role + permission + branch, since a permission is released to a branch once
operations.purpose: Release a permission to a branch so its School Admin may grant it.

parameters.name: role_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No role of that name exists.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the roles that match with how many users hold each and how many permissions each carries.

parameters.notes: The role the permission belongs to.

parameters.name: permission_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such permission, or the role does not hold it.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the permissions this role holds with the module each belongs to.

parameters.notes: The permission being released. It must be one the role holds (BR-1).

parameters.name: release_branch_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the branches with their codes.

parameters.notes: The branch it is released to. A School Admin there may then grant it, within their own branch and to roles at or below their own (BR-3).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Who can now hand this out, and to whom.

fields.name: release_id
fields.description: The release.

fields.name: permission
fields.description: What was released.

fields.name: branch
fields.description: Where it was released to.

fields.name: grantable_by
fields.description: That branch's School Admin, within their own branch and only to roles at or below their own (BR-3, E2, E3).

fields.name: nobody_gained_it
fields.description: True. Releasing makes a permission grantable, not granted (BR-3).

fields.name: role_hierarchy
fields.description: Which roles count as at or below a School Admin's own is **not defined anywhere** — the delegation rule depends on it and the use case raises it unanswered (BR-3, OQ-1).

errors.meaning: A School Admin attempted to grant a permission not released to their branch.
errors.note: A School Admin cannot grant what the Super Admin has not released (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Say that nobody has gained anything. Releasing makes a permission grantable at that branch; it does not give it to a single person (BR-3).

Say who can now hand it out and to whom. That branch's School Admin may grant it to anybody at or below their own role, without asking the Super Admin again — which is the point and also the exposure (BR-2, BR-3).
Say that the hierarchy this depends on is undefined. "Roles at or below their own" is the whole limit on delegation and nothing in the system defines the ordering (BR-3, OQ-1).
Never release to more branches than were asked for. Each is a campus where a School Admin can hand this out unsupervised (BR-3).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: The use case describes releasing a permission to a branch and describes no withdrawal of a release. Anything a School Admin granted while it was released stays granted, so this is a decision worth making once carefully (BR-3).

request.text: fee ledger ki permission Johar Town ko release kar dein
request.gloss: release the fee ledger permission to Johar Town

resolvedPlans.outcome: Released. Nobody has gained it — Johar Town's School Admin can now hand it to anybody at or below their own role there, without asking again. Two things worth saying: which roles count as at or below their own is defined nowhere in the system, and the use case describes releasing and describes no way to withdraw a release.

intent.name: role.deactivate
intent.summary: Retire a role nobody holds. It stays readable, because the audit trail references it.

routesHere.text: ye purana role band kar dein, koi ise nahi rakhta
routesHere.gloss: deactivate this old role, nobody holds it

request.gloss: delete the role entirely

routesElsewhere.note: There is no delete. The audit trail references the role, and every entry recording what somebody did under it would point at nothing (BR-8, E9).

request.gloss: users still hold it, deactivate it anyway

routesElsewhere.note: It is refused while any user holds it, since a user with no role can do nothing (BR-8, E8, A5). They are reassigned first.

operations.name: role.deactivate
operations.idempotencyKey: role_id, since a role is deactivated once and a repeat is the same state
operations.purpose: Deactivate a role that no user holds.

parameters.name: role_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active role of that name exists.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the roles that match with how many users hold each and how many permissions each carries.

parameters.notes: The role, named the way the school names it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: role_id
fields.description: The role.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Deactivated. Never deleted (BR-8, E9).

fields.name: users_holding_it
fields.description: Must be zero. A user left with no role can do nothing, so they are reassigned first (BR-8, E8, A5).

fields.name: audit_entries_referencing_it
fields.description: Entries recording what people did while holding this role. They stay readable because the role does (BR-8).

fields.name: released_permissions
fields.description: Branches this role's permissions were released to. Nothing here withdraws a release, and the use case describes none (BR-3).

fields.name: permissions
fields.description: What it held, kept on the record.

errors.note: They are reassigned first — a user with no role can do nothing (BR-8).

errors.meaning: Deletion was attempted rather than deactivation.
errors.note: The audit trail references the role (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Say who still holds it before anything else. The deactivation is refused while a single user does, and each of them has to be moved to another role first — a user left with none can do nothing at all (BR-8, E8, A5).
Say that nothing is removed. Every audit entry recording what somebody did while holding this role needs the role to stay readable (BR-8, E9).
Name the branches its permissions were released to. Nothing withdraws a release and the use case describes no route for it, so those releases outlive the role (BR-3).

reversal.statement: It is brought back into use with its permission set intact. Nothing was lost (BR-8).

request.text: purana exam office ka role band kar dein
request.gloss: deactivate the old exam office role

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, 3 users still hold it.

steps.note: Refused on the users holding it (PR-1).

Note also that this role's permissions were released to two branches and nothing withdraws a release — those outlive the role.

intent.name: role.reactivate

operations.name: role.reactivate

operations.purpose: Bring a deactivated role back into use.

parameters.name: role_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No deactivated role of that name exists. Deactivated roles are named here just as active ones are.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the roles that match with how many users hold each and how many permissions each carries.

parameters.notes: The role, named the way the school names it.

parameters.name: branch_id

fields.name: role_id
fields.description: The role.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Active.

fields.name: permissions
fields.description: Exactly what it held when it was retired. Nothing revisits them on the way back (BR-1).

fields.name: permission_count
fields.description: How many, which is worth reading against what the role is being brought back to do (BR-1).

fields.name: released_to_branches

fields.name: users_holding_it

errors.meaning: No deactivated role of that name exists.

Say that nobody holds it. The role had to be empty before it could be retired, so bringing it back grants nothing to anybody until somebody is assigned to it at a branch (BR-2, BR-7, BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Answer "what can this role do" with the permissions, not with the menu. What a role reaches is what these permissions say — the menu is decoration over addresses anybody can type (BR-4, BR-5, E5).
Answer the permission question both ways round. "Which roles can see salaries" is the question that finds the role nobody meant to give it to, and it is not answerable from a list of roles (BR-1).

Say which permissions are released to which branches. Those are the ones a School Admin can hand out without asking the Super Admin again, and they are invisible in a plain list of what a role holds (BR-3).
Give holders by branch. One person may hold different roles at different campuses, so a count of holders is not a count of people (BR-7, A4).
Name the roles nobody holds. Each one is still grantable and still carries whatever it accumulated, and nothing surfaces them (BR-1, BR-8).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: salary dekhne ki permission kis kis role ke paas hai?
request.gloss: which roles hold the salary viewing permission?

steps.note: The question asked from the permission's side (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give every role holding it with the number of people in each, by branch. Then the part that matters more: which of those roles have this permission **released to a branch**, because at those campuses a School Admin can hand the role — and therefore salary visibility — to anybody at or below their own role without asking again.

request.text: Coordinator role kya kya kar sakta hai?
request.gloss: what can the Coordinator role do?

resolvedPlans.outcome: List the permissions by module — that is what the role can reach, on the server, on every request, whether the user goes through the menu or types the address. Give the holders by branch, and say which of these permissions are released to which branches, since those are the ones a School Admin can pass on without asking anybody.
